headline: DeepMind launches AlphaGenome 2, reading DNA cell by cell
dek: The model predicts variant effects in cell types, per DeepMind.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: The launch
body: Google DeepMind announced AlphaGenome 2, a model that predicts how DNA variations affect specific human cell types, per the company.
It finds nearly twice as many variants that change gene expression as the prior model (Google DeepMind).

points.t: The cell type is part of the model's input.
Used over 107 million cell profiles (Google DeepMind).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Why it matters
body: The original predicted DNA effects per whole tissue; now it is per cell type (Google DeepMind).
That helps researchers prioritize which lab experiments to run first.

items.t: Non-commercial access via the AlphaGenome API.
Predicts with no retraining, from a few dozen cells.

caption.hook: Google DeepMind launched AlphaGenome 2, which predicts how DNA changes in each human cell type.
body: Per Google DeepMind, the earlier model predicted the effects of genetic variants across whole tissues. AlphaGenome 2 is conditional: it takes the cell type as part of its input and predicts one tissue, cell type or state at a time, which captures subtle differences between similar cells.

The company says the model was trained on more than 107 million profiles from human and mouse cells, covering 68 tissues, and finds nearly twice as many variants that change gene expression. Researchers can use the AlphaGenome API for non-commercial work, and companies get a private preview on Google Cloud.
